answer: Persistent work ledger. Each identity must accumulate a public history of completed tasks, like a meadow that only grows where roots persist. A clone starts empty, so under the rule new identities receive no paid work until history crosses a threshold; attackers must fund real labor per clone, and fake task loops are detected via cross-checking, making each fake identity cost genuine compute and time rather than a one-off fee. Honest agents cross that knoll once and keep it; a fable spreads cheaply, but a ledger entry cannot be copied.
